name: ANSI/IEEE functional equipotential bonding symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented functional equipotential bond used to keep equipment at a common reference for operation or noise control.
description: A functional equipotential bond ties equipment together for operational reasons, such as keeping communications equipment at a common reference or reducing high-frequency noise. The publisher's IEEE miscellaneous preview lists a functional equipotential bond form, the counterpart of the existing IEC concept page.

This illustration is an independent explanation and not the IEEE graphic. A functional bond does not satisfy protective bonding requirements unless it is also sized and installed as a protective conductor. Drawings should not use the functional form where a safety bond is intended.
readingNotes: Do not treat a functional bond as a protective one.
Check high-frequency bonding requirements for drives and comms.
drawingChecklist: State the reason for the functional bond.
Size it separately from protective bonds.
distinction: A functional bond supports operation; a protective bond provides safety during faults.
